details: German law requires you to register your address at the local Bürgeramt (Citizens' Office) within 2 weeks of arrival. You need your passport, rental contract, and a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung (landlord confirmation form). Go to Birkenfeld Rathaus.

Go to the IT ServicePoint in Building 9917 with your enrollment letter. They will set up your university email address and help with your first login. All official communication from the university goes there.
Collect your physical student ID card from the Studierendensekretariat (Building 9924). You need this for the library, many campus services, and transport-related student discounts.

International students must have German health insurance. If you are under 30 and enrolled full-time, you qualify for public insurance (TK, AOK, DAK). Visit a local branch or register online. You need proof of insurance to stay enrolled.

task: Log in to Stud.IP and QIS
details: Stud.IP is the learning platform (courses, files, announcements). QIS is the exam registration system. Your login credentials are the same for both. Find your courses and join them on Stud.IP.

You need a German bank account to receive your BAföG, scholarships, or work salary. DKB and N26 offer free accounts with an English interface. Bring your passport, registration certificate (Anmeldebestätigung), and enrollment letter.

task: Apply for a semester ticket (if applicable)
details: Your student fee (Semesterbeitrag) includes a regional transport ticket. Check the AStA website for the coverage area and how to activate it on your student card.
The International Office can help with visa extensions, recognition of foreign certificates, and general support for international students. They often speak English.

Exam registration is done through the QIS portal. Registration periods are typically 4–6 weeks before exams. Check exact dates in the academic calendar. Missing the registration deadline means you cannot sit the exam.
